artifacts.note: Engineering vertical slice: adaptive loop beats static and random under simulation. Not a human efficacy result.
Historical pilot gate (2/6 passes). Its VALIDATED label is not canonical; P2R establishes that the confirmatory cohort was not executed.
Spatial-provenance blocker; resolved in method, not in data.
Canonical: confirmatory compute blocked; 1/6 subjects preprocessed; no neural outcome computed. Imagery remains unauthorized.

Planning check for N=180 with 2,000 simulations. Power for true ICC 0.75 with lower 95% bound above 0.60 is 0.961 under a normal approximation. Not human evidence; the registered analysis will use the actual ICC confidence-interval method.

Stage 0 simulation with 120 simulated participants and 120 trials each. Parameter recovery passed (bias +0.051, RMSE 0.197). Adaptive EIG reduced final posterior entropy by 28.9% versus the fixed stratified schedule. This is a design artifact, not human evidence.
Planning check for N=180 with 2,000 simulations. Power for true ICC 0.75 with lower 95% bound above 0.60 is 0.961 under a normal approximation. Not human evidence.

Policy-parameter recovery with 60 simulated participants and 80 trials. Beta bias -0.131, lambda bias -0.035, tau bias -0.025. Conditional on the known EIG feature matrix; not a human validation and not a full hierarchical recovery.

Stage 0B simulation with 120 simulated participants and 120 trials, four cards and at most two samples per trial. Mean accuracy 0.458, mean ARTE 0.444, and mean queries 1.79. This is a design artifact, not human evidence.
Null on incremental behavioural validity; mechanism unresolved because temporal and channel controls reproduce the effect.
Null content and transfer result within sensitivity; compact architectures at or below chance under LOSO.
Perception decoding passes; zero-shot imagery transfer is null within sensitivity; reconstruction readiness blocked.
Earlier real-data decision blocked by unresolved imagery row provenance. Preserved unmodified; superseded after the NSD row mapping was resolved.
Cross-session alignment restores seen-image decoding but imagery remains degenerate (dominant fraction 0.510). Single subject, not population evidence.
Execution-incomplete blocker; superseded by the completed run.
Perception-estimand blocker; superseded by the completed run.
One of six subjects passes; C3XAG preparation is not authorized. This is a limited result, not a validation.

claims.effect: Engineering vertical slice; no human validation
claims.statement: The platform can scaffold scene authoring and adaptive behavioural practice and can report uncertainty, without claiming that it improves imagery strength or clinical outcomes.
claims.uncertainty: No psychometric validation, no efficacy estimate

claims.statement: Scene Threshold estimates a within-scene 2-AFC discrimination threshold and d-prime with calibrated uncertainty.
claims.uncertainty: No test-retest, convergent, or known-groups validation in humans

claims.effect: C3XAT-R1 passed 1 of 6 subjects; not a validation
claims.statement: The epistemic interview reconstructs probe-variable beliefs with reported uncertainty, not a picture of what a person imagined.

claims.effect: 2 of 6 pilot passes; confirmatory cohort not executed
claims.statement: A perception-trained decoder can recover seen-image content above chance in a held-out subject under the sealed ANIMUS protocol.
claims.uncertainty: No confirmatory estimate; P2R blocked on compute

claims.effect: C3 and C3M null; C3XAT-R1 pass in 1/6 subjects
claims.statement: A decoder can recover imagined scene content above chance from held-out neural data, beyond session, cue, and state confounds.
claims.uncertainty: Single-subject evidence; degenerate predictions in the imagery arm

claims.statement: Imagery-related neural geometry can be estimated and used to authorize a new acquisition or closed-loop geometry experiment.
PID and IQI are composite proxy scores that summarize simulated or demonstrated session signals.
The platform diagnoses, treats, or clinically validates a mental-health or neurological condition.
claims.uncertainty: No clinical study, no regulatory review

claims.statement: The Source and Imagination Monitor estimates source discrimination and source calibration for seen, imagined, described, and new content, with reported uncertainty and explicit insufficient-data states.
claims.uncertainty: Stage 0 specification and simulation only; no human reliability or validity data

claims.statement: Active Reality Testing estimates the efficiency with which a person selects source-diagnostic evidence before judging whether an experience was seen, imagined, described, or new, with reported uncertainty and explicit insufficient-data states.
claims.uncertainty: Stage 0B specification and simulation only; no human reliability or validity data

claims.statement: Adaptive Active Reality Testing feedback improves source-inquiry efficiency or source calibration beyond a yoked active control.
claims.uncertainty: Conditional on measurement validation; no training RCT has been executed

claims.statement: Active Reality Testing diagnoses, predicts, or treats a clinical condition.
claims.uncertainty: No clinical sample, no diagnostic accuracy study, no regulatory review

claims.statement: Adaptive source-monitoring feedback improves source calibration or source discrimination beyond a yoked active control.
claims.uncertainty: Conditional on measurement validation; no training RCT has been executed

claims.statement: The Source and Imagination Monitor diagnoses, predicts, or treats a clinical condition.
claims.uncertainty: No clinical sample, no diagnostic accuracy study, no regulatory review

gates.name: Neural-behavioural alignment
gates.note: Null on incremental validity; mechanism unresolved.

gates.name: Neural content and state disentanglement
gates.note: Null content and transfer within sensitivity.

gates.name: Cross-session alignment mechanism
gates.note: Alignment works for seen images; imagery remains degenerate.

gates.name: ANIMUS closed-loop vertical slice
gates.note: Engineering pass under simulation; not a human validation.

gates.name: Source-monitoring Stage 0 simulation
gates.note: Simulation-only design gate for the Source and Imagination Monitor. A PASS means parameter recovery and the coverage constraints are acceptable in simulation; it is not human validation and does not authorize a measurement claim.

gates.name: Source-monitoring Stage 1 power check
gates.note: Simulation-only planning gate. A PASS means the planned N=180 has at least 80% power for the reliability lower-bound target under the stated approximation; it is not human evidence.

gates.name: Active Reality Testing Stage 0B simulation
gates.note: Simulation-only design gate. A PASS means the EIG agent is above chance and its query choices are efficient under the stated model; it is not human validation and does not authorize a measurement claim.

gates.name: Active Reality Testing Stage 2 power check
gates.note: Simulation-only planning gate. A PASS means N=180 has at least 80% power for the ARTE reliability lower-bound target under the stated approximation; it is not human evidence.

gates.name: Active Reality Testing policy recovery
gates.note: Simulation-only model-recovery gate. A PASS means the policy parameters are recovered within the stated tolerance conditional on the known EIG feature matrix; it does not validate the task or the full hierarchical measurement model.
